analysis.title: Opera Ltd. (OPRA) Q3'26 Earnings Review: Near-Term Focus Remains on AI & Advertising Growth Vectors
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on OPRA and cuts the 12-month price target to $21.50 from $24.00 (39.6% upside from $15.40), citing lower forward operating estimates and management's forward commentary.

Q3'26 revenue of $183mm and adjusted EBITDA of $43mm came in at or above the high end of guidance ($181-183mm and $41-43mm). Revenue was in line with GS ($182mm) and consensus ($183mm). EPS was $0.30 vs GS $0.28 and consensus $0.30.
Q3 growth was broad: Advertising +22% YoY to $117mm and Query +17% YoY to $65mm. ARPU rose 22% YoY.

The Q4 guide implies slower sequential revenue growth. Management cites tough YoY comps and eCommerce returning to a more normal seasonal pattern. Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $46mm is below GS and Street expectations.
Cost of revenue is expected to rise 5-6 percentage points YoY in Q4 from growth investments in gaming and CTV, partly offset by opex leverage.
Management expects the softer eCommerce growth seen in Q3 to persist beyond the quarter, which it attributes to new cross-border regulation.

Advertising is diversifying beyond eCommerce. Gaming is now a double-digit percentage of ad revenue, travel is growing faster than the broader ad business, and CTV/cross-channel inventory has shown early encouraging results.
User metrics: desktop MAUs reached a record 100mm in October (+16% YoY), Opera One iOS users rose 20% YoY in October, Opera GX added over 4mm MAUs YoY, and Western market MAUs rose 1mm YoY.
Management is focusing on local AI (Web AI), bringing open-weight models onto users' devices, while keeping an interoperable approach across local and cloud models.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin was 24% and FCF conversion 75%. Capital allocation centers on growth investment, buybacks and dividends.
GS expects investors to focus on the ad environment and revenue growth into 2027, and on whether gaming, travel and CTV can offset slower eCommerce growth.

Estimate changes: Q4'26 revenue $202mm (from $204mm), adjusted EBITDA $46mm (from $48mm), EPS $0.26 (from $0.33). FY26 EPS $1.14 (from $1.18). FY27 revenue unchanged at $844mm, adjusted EBITDA $201mm (from $200mm), EPS $1.42 (from $1.41).
FY27 advertising revenue estimate falls 2.5% to $544mm and FY28 falls 4.2% to $612mm, while FY27 Query revenue rises 4.7% to $297mm and FY28 rises 8.1% to $338mm.

The price target blends 7.5x EV/GAAP EBITDA (from 9.0x) on NTM+1 year estimates with a modified DCF at 11.0x EV/FCF-SBC (from 13.5x) on NTM+4 year estimates, discounted 3 years at 12%. Scenario values are $10.50 downside, $21.50 base and $26.00 upside.
The stock is down 24.2% over 3 months and 13.9% over 6 months, and is up 14.4% over 12 months. It trails the Russell 2000 by 15.3% over 3 months.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Buy and cuts the price target from $24.00 to $21.50 on lower forward GAAP estimates and a lower valuation multiple. Q3 was at the high end of guidance, but the Q4 EBITDA guide is below expectations.

earnings_insights: OPRA Q3'26 reported (company data): revenue $183mm vs GS $182mm and consensus $183mm, guidance $181-183mm. Advertising $117mm (+22% YoY), Query $65mm (+17% YoY).
OPRA Q3'26 adjusted EBITDA reported $43mm (23.6% margin) vs GS $42mm and consensus $43mm, guidance $41-43mm. GAAP EBITDA was $40mm vs GS estimate $34mm.
OPRA Q3'26 EPS reported $0.30 vs GS estimate $0.28 and consensus $0.30.

OPRA Q4'26 company guidance: revenue $198-205mm and adjusted EBITDA $44-47mm. GS new estimates are revenue $202mm, adjusted EBITDA $46mm (GS estimate, from $48mm) and EPS $0.26 (from $0.33). GS says the Q4 adjusted EBITDA guide came in below GS and Street expectations.
GS FY26 estimates: revenue $739mm (guidance $735-742mm), adjusted EBITDA $173mm (guidance $172-175mm), EPS $1.14 (from $1.18). FY27 GS estimates: revenue $844mm, adjusted EBITDA $201mm, EPS $1.42.
risk_factors: Slowdown in industry advertising spend from macroeconomic volatility.
Competition for users from other desktop and mobile browsers, and for advertising dollars.
Execution risk on western market penetration and adoption of newer products (GX, Aria).

Concentrated governance: the Chairman and co-CEO holds majority voting power, a majority shareholder owns over 70% of shares, and the Chairman is also CEO of OPay, in which Opera holds a minority stake.
Regulatory and geopolitical exposure from operations in Mainland China.
Softer eCommerce advertising growth persisting after Q3.
Growth investments in gaming and CTV pressuring near-term margins.
geopolitical: The report names a new cross-border regulation as the cause of softer eCommerce advertising growth in Q3, which management expects to persist beyond the quarter.
Risk disclosure: presence in Mainland China, where the majority shareholder, certain directors and R&D operations are based, creates possible regulatory and geopolitical exposure.
